newsitem.title: USA: DLJ Q3 underwriting revs fall on weak market.
newsitem.headline: DLJ Q3 underwriting revs fall on weak market.

text.p: Donaldson Lufkin & Jenrette Inc said a somewhat weaker market for new issues in the third quarter contributed to an 11 percent decline in underwriting revenues.
It said third quarter underwriting revenues fell to $130 million from $146 million a year earlier.
DLJ said that as of September 30, it ranked fourth in disclosed underwriting fees earned from domestic public new issues in the United States.

DLJ said third quarter fee income increased 38 percent versus the comparable quarter a year ago to a record $125 million, as a result of record investment banking fees and continued momentum in the development of the firm's merger and acqusition business.
DLJ reported higher third quarter and nine month earnings and revenues earlier Tuesday. The firm is 80 percent beneficially owned by Equitable Cos Inc.
